Run traces, token accounting and reports (BB-098); direct-versus-supervised experiment and suite (BB-099).

constraints: New private workspace package packages/agent-tools (@exharness/agent-tools, type module, node >=20) with no runtime npm dependencies; it imports Core from ../../core-harness/src/index.js and the BB-096 adapters from ../../agentic-system/src/index.js, the same relative convention packages/agentic-system uses.

Every process is started with spawn and an argument array and shell:false; on win32 an npm .cmd/.ps1 shim is resolved to its JavaScript entry and run with process.execPath, and cmd.exe/powershell are never used.

Every test in the package is titled with its criterion prefix (AT1..AT4 followed by a space), declares { timeout: 60000 }, uses only fake CLIs and temp git repositories, and removes worktrees and temp dirs in finally blocks.

Root package.json gains test:agent-tools (node --test packages/agent-tools/test/*.test.js) appended to the test script, and smoke:agent-tools (node packages/agent-tools/bin/exharness-agent.mjs smoke) which is not part of test or verify.
Adapters are not a sandbox; docs must state that live runs execute with the user's CLI permissions inside a temp worktree only and point isolation to BB-067.
Research only in this lane: no product source edits, no self-issued readiness or fabricated Jev judgment.
invariants: Only a candidate whose declared verifications all PASS at its exact commit can be promoted; the agent exit status or message never contributes to acceptance.
Agent processes run only in an isolated worktree under os.tmpdir(); the source repository HEAD, branches and working tree are never modified.
No process is started through a shell, and every agent invocation is bounded by a timeout that kills its process tree.
User CLI configuration and credentials are never read or written by the adapters.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Files: packages/agent-tools/{package.json, src/index.js, src/tool-adapters.js, src/process-runner.js, src/supervisor.js, bin/exharness-agent.mjs, test/agent-tools.test.js, test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs}. Root exports: defineAgentTool, codexTool, kiroTool, agyTool, runAgentInvocation, createSupervisedAgentStrategy, runSupervisedTask, AgentTaskStatus.

D2 — AGENT_TOOL_ADAPTER_V1 = { id, command, prefixArgs = [], versionArgs, buildInvocation({ prompt, resume, model, permissionProfile, logFile }) -> { args, stdin }, parseResult({ exitCode, stdout, stderr }) -> { claimedSuccess, finalMessage } }. defineAgentTool(base, { command, prefixArgs }) overrides only the executable so tests can substitute a fake while keeping the real argument builder.

D3 — Invocations (flags confirmed by the executed probe): codex first = [exec, --json, --skip-git-repo-check, --sandbox, <workspace-write|danger-full-access>, (--model m), -] with prompt on stdin, resume = [exec, resume, --last, --json, -] with prompt on stdin; kiro first = [chat, --no-interactive, <--trust-tools=fs_read,fs_write,execute_bash | --trust-all-tools>, (--model m), <prompt>], resume adds --resume; agy first = [--print, <prompt>, --mode, accept-edits (or --dangerously-skip-permissions for FULL_AUTO), (--model m), --log-file, <path>], resume adds --continue. Permission profiles are WORKSPACE_EDIT (default) and FULL_AUTO (explicit opt-in). The process cwd is always the worktree root.

D4 — runAgentInvocation(tool, request, { cwd, timeoutMs = 600000, maxOutputBytes = 1048576 }) spawns tool.command with [...prefixArgs, ...args], writes stdin when present, captures stdout/stderr up to maxOutputBytes (recording truncation), and on timeout kills the process tree (POSIX: detached + process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL"); win32: taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F via execFile). It returns { exitCode, signal, timedOut, durationMs, stdout, stderr, stdoutSha256, stderrSha256, truncated }. A missing executable (ENOENT) returns TOOL_UNAVAILABLE without throwing.

D5 — Supervisor: runSupervisedTask({ tool, task, maxAttempts = 3, timeoutMs, maxFeedbackChars = 8000, permissionProfile, eventSinks = [], tracer = null }) creates a BB-096 createLocalGitWorkspace at task.baseRevision and BB-096 createLocalCommandVerifier instances for task.verifications (requireUnchangedTree true). It composes createHarness({ strategy: createSupervisedAgentStrategy(...), environment: workspace, verifiers, verificationPolicy requiring every declared verifier, objective, eventSinks, tracer }).

D6 — Attempt loop inside strategy.run({ input, invoke }): attempt 1 prompt = task.prompt; attempt n>1 prompt = task.prompt + a bounded feedback block listing each failing verifier name, status, reason and output tail (total <= maxFeedbackChars), invoked with resume. After each invocation: if HEAD moved, `git reset --soft <candidate.version>` and record AGENT_COMMITS_FOLDED; edits = every added/modified path from `git status --porcelain` read from the worktree; invoke ACT (BB-096 act commits, staging deletions via git add -A); invoke every verification capability; invoke EVALUATE; PASS -> PROMOTE and return ACCEPTED. mutated false is recorded as NO_CHANGE and counts as an attempt. After maxAttempts return EXHAUSTED.

D7 — objective.evaluate returns PASS only when Core-supplied verifications for the current candidate contain a PASS record for every declared verifier; tool claimedSuccess/finalMessage are stored in the attempt record only.

D8 — AGENT_TASK_V1 = { id, repositoryRoot, baseRevision (40-hex), prompt, verifications: [{ name, command, args, timeoutMs }] } validated before any process starts. AGENT_SUPERVISED_RESULT_V1 = { taskId, tool, toolVersion, status ACCEPTED|EXHAUSTED|TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, attempts: [{ index, resume, exitCode, timedOut, durationMs, claimedSuccess, candidateSha, mutated, foldedAgentCommits, verification: [{ name, status, reason }], feedbackChars }], acceptedSha }.

D9 — bin/exharness-agent.mjs: `run --tool <codex|kiro|agy> --task <task.json> [--max-attempts N] [--timeout-ms T] [--permission WORKSPACE_EDIT|FULL_AUTO]` prints AGENT_SUPERVISED_RESULT_V1; `probe` prints versions; `smoke --tool <t>` creates a temp repo with one failing test and a one-line fix prompt, runs the supervised loop and prints the result, or prints SKIPPED with reason NOT_INSTALLED or TOOL_FAILED_BEFORE_EDIT; it never reports ACCEPTED without a passing verification.

D10 — Fake CLI fixture test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs selects behavior from env FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO: FIX_FIRST, FIX_AFTER_FEEDBACK (writes the fix only when its prompt contains the verification failure text), NEVER_FIX, CLAIM_SUCCESS_NO_EDIT, SELF_COMMIT, HANG. It records the argv and stdin it received to a JSON file for argv assertions.

D11 — Evidence basis: executed probe shows all three CLIs installed with non-interactive, resume and permission flags; only codex has --json; no ExHarness code launches external agents; BB-066 names only OpenHands.
implementationSlices: S1 — Adapters [AT1]: implement D2-D3. "AT1 ..." tests assert exact first/resume argv and stdin per tool and profile, that a prompt containing `; & | " $()` reaches the fake verbatim, that a missing executable yields TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, and that the win32 shim resolver returns process.execPath + a .js entry (tested with a synthetic shim directory).

S2 — Process runner [AT2]: implement D4. "AT2 ..." tests cover exit code capture, output truncation flag and digests, and HANG with timeoutMs 500 returning timedOut within 10s with the pid no longer alive.

S3 — Supervisor [AT3]: implement D5-D8. "AT3 ..." tests on temp git repos cover FIX_FIRST -> ACCEPTED in 1 attempt; FIX_AFTER_FEEDBACK -> ACCEPTED in 2 attempts with resume argv and feedback text observed by the fake; NEVER_FIX -> EXHAUSTED after maxAttempts with no PROMOTE; CLAIM_SUCCESS_NO_EDIT -> not ACCEPTED with NO_CHANGE; SELF_COMMIT -> folded into one candidate; source repository unchanged in every case.

S4 — CLI + smoke + docs [AT4]: implement D9-D10. "AT4 ..." tests run the bin `run` against the fake tool and parse the result, and `smoke` with a nonexistent tool command yields SKIPPED NOT_INSTALLED. Add root scripts, write docs/living/system/agent-tools/state.md and link it from docs/living/system/state.md, then run test:agent-tools, verify:current-docs and npm test.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: Specify tool adapters for Codex, Kiro and agy that build exact shell-free non-interactive and resume invocations with explicit permission profiles, resolve Windows npm shims without cmd.exe, and report an unavailable tool as TOOL_UNAVAILABLE.
Specify one bounded process runner that captures bounded output with digests, redacts nothing it does not own, and terminates the whole process tree on timeout.

Specify an ExHarness-supervised loop on Core createHarness and the BB-096 workspace/verifiers where each agent invocation is an ACT candidate, only passing declared verification can PROMOTE, failures feed back through tool resume up to maxAttempts, agent commits are folded into one candidate and the agent claim is telemetry only.
Specify a CLI entrypoint and an opt-in live smoke that never fakes success when a tool is missing or unauthenticated, plus Living docs stating the no-sandbox trust boundary.

negativeVerificationCases: A prompt containing shell metacharacters is received verbatim by the fake tool and never interpreted.
A missing tool executable yields TOOL_UNAVAILABLE and no attempt is recorded as ACCEPTED.
A hung tool invocation is killed at timeoutMs and its process tree is no longer alive.
A tool that exits 0 and claims success without editing is not ACCEPTED (NO_CHANGE).
A tool that never fixes the task ends EXHAUSTED after exactly maxAttempts with no PROMOTE.
A tool that commits on its own has its commits folded into exactly one candidate commit.
After any scenario the source repository HEAD, branch list and porcelain status are unchanged.
smoke with an unavailable tool prints SKIPPED and never ACCEPTED.
Any write to packages/core-harness, packages/oracle, packages/agentic-system or docs/blackboard fails scope verification.
